claims.text: A partial solar eclipse was witnessed across parts of Africa on August 12, 2026.
The next total solar eclipse visible from the UK, France, and mainland Europe will take place in September 2081.
European Space Agency reserve astronaut Sara García Alonso told RTVE that the eclipse was one of the most beautiful things she had ever seen and gave her goosebumps.
Astronaut Pablo Álvarez Fernández stated that the eclipse was much more beautiful than he had expected.
Thousands of people gathered across Spain, Iceland, and other European countries on August 12, 2026, to watch a total solar eclipse.
The total solar eclipse was Spain's first in more than a century.
Spanish authorities expected at least 500,000 additional visitors for the solar eclipse.
Spain deployed more than 33,500 law enforcement officers around eclipse viewing areas and access points.
Iceland experienced its first total solar eclipse since 1954, which was visible from Reykjavík for the first time since 1433.
The total solar eclipse started at 15:34 GMT on August 12, 2026, with totality lasting about two minutes.
The path of totality brought near-total darkness to approximately 15 million people across northern Russia, Greenland, Iceland, Spain, and part of Portugal.
The solar eclipse was the first total eclipse visible in mainland Europe since 2006.
The Spanish government estimated that 450,000 extra tourists visiting for the eclipse would provide a 347-million-euro ($400 million) economic boost.
Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska stated that nearly 25,000 police officers were mobilised for the eclipse.
Another total solar eclipse is expected to cross southern Spain and northern Africa in August 2027, followed by an annular eclipse over the Iberian Peninsula in 2028.
White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt will step down from her position at the end of August 2026.
President Donald Trump wrote in a social media post that Leavitt will become one of his top outside advisors and an influential voice within the Republican Party.
Karoline Leavitt, aged 28, became the youngest person to ever serve as White House Press Secretary when she took the role.
Leavitt gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Viviana, with husband Nicholas Riccio in May 2026.
In 2022, Leavitt won a Republican primary but lost the general election for a New Hampshire Congressional seat to Democrat Chris Pappas.
In February 2025, Leavitt's office seized control of the White House press pool from the White House Correspondents' Association.
President Trump signed a national security presidential memorandum on August 12, 2026, to empower federal law enforcement to use cyber tools against transnational criminal organizations.
During a briefing on January 28, 2025, Leavitt incorrectly claimed that DOGE and OMB found $50 million in federal funds slated for condoms in Gaza.
The Washington Post reported that Trump used a plane carrying cabinet officials, staff, and journalists as a decoy when leaving a NATO summit in Turkey in July 2026 due to an assassination threat.
Leavitt delayed her maternity leave in May 2026 following an alleged assassination attempt on Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.
Four senior female Cabinet-level officials—Kristi Noem, Pam Bondi, Lori Chavez-DeRemer, and Tulsi Gabbard—departed Trump's second administration by mid-2026.
Kristi Noem was fired as Secretary of Homeland Security on March 5, 2026, and was succeeded by Senator Markwayne Mullin.
Attorney General Pam Bondi was ousted in early April 2026 amid controversy over Jeffrey Epstein files and was replaced by Todd Blanche.
Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer resigned on April 20, 2026, amid an internal fraud and misconduct investigation.
Tulsi Gabbard left her post as Director of National Intelligence effective June 30, 2026, and was replaced by Jay Clayton.
A 32-year-old woman named Daniela Largo was rescued alive in Pereira after being trapped under rubble for 36 hours following a 7.4-magnitude earthquake in Colombia.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella stated that at least 265 people died and 496 remain missing following the earthquake.
According to Asocapitales, 79 people died in Pereira and 95 died in Cali following the earthquake.
At least 92 buildings collapsed in Pereira during the earthquake.
The 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia at 07:34 local time (12:34 GMT) on August 10, 2026, with its epicenter near San José del Palmar in Chocó province.
Search and rescue operations continued in Colombia as thousands were reported missing after the earthquake.
More than 200 people were confirmed dead and over 2,000 reported missing 48 hours after the earthquake in Colombia.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency following the earthquake.
Daniela Largo was rescued from the ruins of a collapsed hotel in Pereira after spending 36 hours under debris.
Tata Sons Chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran announced he will step down at the end of his tenure in February 2027.
Chandrasekaran worked at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) for 30 years starting in 1987, serving as CEO from 2009 to 2017 before becoming Tata Sons chairman in January 2017.
Noel Tata became chairman of Tata Trusts in October 2024 following the death of Ratan Tata.
Tata Trusts controls a 66% stake in Tata Sons.
Chandrasekaran stated he decided to step down because Tata Sons board member Noel Tata did not support extending his term for a third five-year period.
The Shapoorji Pallonji Group holds approximately an 18% stake in Tata Sons.
The Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) is currently unable to convene trustee meetings due to a directive from the Maharashtra charity commissioner.
Tata Sons amended its articles of association in 2022 to bar the Tata Trusts chairman from simultaneously serving as Tata Sons chairman.
Tata Steel Managing Director TV Narendran is being considered among candidates to replace Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman.
Chandrasekaran received a total remuneration of ₹158.66 crore from Tata Sons for FY26, including ₹140.69 crore in profit-linked commission.
Chandrasekaran earned a cumulative ₹671.4 crore in remuneration from Tata Sons between FY22 and FY26.
Former Tata Sons Chairman Ratan Tata died on October 9, 2024, at the age of 86.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun stated on August 12, 2026, that the China-India border situation is generally stable at the moment.
Military standoffs and face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops emerged in the Taksing area of Upper Subansiri district in Arunachal Pradesh in early July 2026.
Military clashes in the Galwan Valley in June 2020 resulted in the deaths of 20 Indian soldiers and at least four Chinese soldiers.
India's Ministry of External Affairs assigned standard Indian names to 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh.
India and China reached a disengagement agreement covering friction points at Depsang and Demchok in October 2024.
India and China held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs in New Delhi on August 6, 2026.
On August 7, 2026, the Indian Union Home Ministry officially issued standard names for 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh.
China claims large parts of Arunachal Pradesh as South Tibet, referring to the region as Zangnan.
